newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end up after quiet day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end up after quiet day.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended higher after a session of light, choppy trading.
Stock indices gleaned no lasting direction from early June producer price index data and spent the session drifting in noncommittal range trade.

The June PPI was the only significant data released all week, and the tame report had scant impact on stock indicies. The overall index fell 0.1 percent and the core rate, which excludes volatile food and energy sectors, rose 0.1 percent.
Traders said action was quiet all day, and September Standard and Poor's 500 futures ended mid-range.
"There was nothing going on here," an S&P 500 futures trader said. "I think it's poised for a rally and we have to wait until next week to get there."
September S&Ps made their most recent record high on Monday, when they charged to 932.25. For the rest of the week they have whipsawed, trading as low as 906.50.
Upside targets remain at the 932.25 high, 935.00 and 937.50.
Traders said a firm Treasury bond futures tone underpinned S&Ps throughout the day. September T-bond futures closed up 8/32 at 114-4/32, in a range from 113-23/32 to 114-15/32.

At the close, Sept S&P 500s were up 2.90 points at 924.40, Nasdaq 100s rose 5.35 to 1026.60, Russell 2000s were up 3.70 points at 407.10, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 130.0 to 19,920.0 and Midcap 400s rose 2.75 points to 302.45.
